report:
# FQ-POSITIVE-WEIGHTS-ADMITTED

The convex Bell argument takes nonnegative weights and a declared total mass. Strict positivity is stronger than required; zero weights are valid. Distinct normalized positive preparations on the same two-label carrier demonstrate nonuniqueness of supplied preparation data, not a universal metatheorem about all distinctions. Signed normalized weights give score6; unnormalized positive weights give score4 at mass2 and obey only the scaled bound.

The universal two-weight rational convex bound is proved with explicit nonnegativity and score bounds; distinct positive normalized preparations, a signed violation and an unnormalized scaled control are checked.

Remaining: Derive a preparation measure from native histories with a stated selection principle. Same-carrier examples only show insufficiency of that bare carrier; no stronger impossibility theorem is claimed.
